articles.title: Why it could take time for a new Israeli government to form
articles.summary: Israel faces what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.
articles.body:
Israelis are voting in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.

It is the first parliamentary election since the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks and subsequent conflicts across the region - in Gaza, Iran, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen.

BBC Middle East correspondent Yolande Knell explains why it may take some time before a new government is formed after the polls close.

articles.title: West in Pictures: 'Winter-ready bear and 'faeries spotted'
articles.summary: Our weekly round-up of photographs from across the West.
articles.body:
Winter preparations are beginning across the West Country as temperatures have started to drop.

Even the Bears at Bristol Zoo Project have been piling on the pounds in preparation for the hibernation season.

Elsewhere, Faeries have been spotted in Glastonbury for the town's annual mythical-themed ball and fayre.

Here is our weekly round-up of photographs from across the region.

Say cheeeeeese: Wallace and Gromit's Grand Appeal, the dedicated charity for Bristol Children's Hospital, has opened a new Gromit Unleashed Shop at Cribbs Mall in time for half term.

Winter coat: Bristol Zoo Project's largest European brown bear, Neo, has piled on 41.5kg since March, tipping the scales at an impressive 365.5kg – more than the combined weight of four animal keepers.

A moment in time: A second photography exhibition celebrating Bristol Royal Hospital for Children's 25th anniversary has been opened and features photography from a former patient documenting those who work at the hospital.

Winter is coming: As the colder months draw in, so do the darker mornings and shorter days. Here is a view from a Bristol resident's conservatory showing the skyline above nearby houses.

Bright futures: The first set of students have embarked on their nurse training as part of a new scheme from Bristol NHS Foundation Trust and BPP University, offering sponsored degree places in Bristol. It gives people who might not have otherwise felt able to undertake a Registered Nursing Degree access to training with financial support.

A place for everyone: Ashton Park School and Sixth Form has been awarded the Inclusion Quality Mark (IQM) Inclusive School Award following a two-day assessment. The school has also achieved prestigious Centre of Excellence status.

Norman history: A replica of the Bayeux Tapestry has gone on display at Tewkesbury Abbey. It is part of a Norman Heritage Trail looking at how the Normans built a new medieval kingdom and reshaped England's landscape, culture and society.

New beginnings: The former Brightlands Day Nursery in Cheltenham has joined the Little Adventures Nursery Group, as part of a £300,000 investment into the site to expand the amount of childcare places it has to offer locals.

That's a wrap: The Times and Sunday Times Cheltenham Literature Festival is over for another year, with organisers saying the 2026 event saw its highest box office sales, with 103,394 tickets bought.

A faerie-fun day: Mystical costumes were out in force in Glastonbury for the town's Faerie Ball and Fayre. It was held at the town hall, with the theme of Green Women.

Wild at heart: About 140 wild Exmoor ponies were rounded up this week for their annual health checks in a tradition dating back nearly a century. Exmoor ponies are one of Britain's oldest native pony breeds, originating from the wild moorlands of Exmoor across Somerset and Devon.

Sharing is caring: A new campaign led by Peasedown St John's Independent Bath and North East Somerset Councillor Karen Walker has seen new signage installed by footpaths that have been designated as shared spaces for cyclists and pedestrians.

Cub named: A new red panda cub at Longleat has been named Sundar, meaning "beautiful" and "handsome" in Nepali. Keepers at Longleat say the cub has also earned his first nickname, Sunny as he is "such a little ray of sunshine to care for".

Sunny spells: Well done to BBC Weather Watchers who managed to dodge the rain this week to take photographs, including Fay C, who captured this picture by the Kennet and Avon Canal in Devizes.

Missing link: After the Mayor of Malmesbury, Robert Hastings, noticed a piece of gold had gone missing from his chain of office, Malmesbury Secondary School has stepped in to create a bespoke replacement made of pewter.

Business recognition: Four Chippenham businesses have celebrated success at the 2026 Female Business Awards in Manchester. Eve Cale, founder of Giftwrapped by Eve; Becky Groves, founder of Rebsey Art Studio; Gabriela Slater, founder of Nu Reflexology; and Helen Osmond, founder of Osmond Education, all received awards.

Autumn leaves: Old Town Gardens in Swindon are awash with autumnal vibes this week, as well as a few added puddles.

articles.title: Jordânia ataca grupos terroristas na Síria após atentado contra igreja; 8 morrem em bombardeios | G1
articles.standfirst: A ofensiva ocorreu após a prisão de três suspeitos de matar nove pessoas e ferir outras 25 durante uma procissão fúnebre. Governo sírio criticou a ação militar sem coordenação prévia.
articles.summary: A ofensiva ocorreu após a prisão de três suspeitos de matar nove pessoas e ferir outras 25 durante uma procissão fúnebre. Governo sírio criticou a ação militar sem coordenação prévia.
articles.body:
Fiéis ouvem um clérigo cristão discursar durante uma vigília na Igreja Ortodoxa Grega da Transfiguração, na Cisjordânia ocupada por Israel, em 26 de outubro de 2026, em solidariedade às vítimas do ataque à Igreja de São Jorge, em 23 de outubro — Foto: ZAIN JAAFAR / AFP

O Exército da Jordânia afirmou que atacou, nesta segunda-feira (26), "organizações terroristas" na vizinha Síria , em retaliação a um atentado jihadista mortal contra uma igreja na semana passada, poucas horas depois de as autoridades prenderem três suspeitos do ataque.

A instituição militar informou que aeronaves da Força Aérea haviam "destruído várias posições terroristas" e matado e ferido "numerosos integrantes" de grupos ligados aos autores do ataque contra a igreja.

O ataque mortal sem precedentes da semana passada contra uma igreja greco-ortodoxa deixou nove mortos e 25 feridos. As forças de segurança da Jordânia prenderam três suspeitos nesta segunda-feira.

A Síria informou que o número de mortos nos ataques desta segunda-feira no sul do país havia subido para oito, ante um balanço anterior de cinco vítimas fatais.

"Os hospitais da província de Daraa receberam oito vítimas, incluindo um idoso e três crianças", além de quatro feridos, informaram as autoridades sanitárias.

O governo sírio afirmou nesta segunda-feira que a Jordânia "não realizou nenhuma coordenação prévia" antes de lançar os ataques mortais em retaliação a um atentado jihadista fatal contra uma igreja, informou a agência estatal de notícias SANA.

A SANA citou o Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Síria , que afirmou ter comunicado à Jordânia sua "completa ressalva quanto à realização de operações em território sírio sem coordenação prévia".

O ministério acrescentou que a "comunicação e a coordenação" com a Jordânia estavam em andamento "para lidar com as repercussões deste incidente de uma maneira que preserve a segurança e a soberania do território sírio".

O rei Abdullah II afirmou que havia "prometido que os terroristas não escapariam da Justiça e que nenhum defensor de ideologias obscurantistas que dividem os jordanianos seria tolerado", escreveu em uma nova publicação na rede social X.

Ataques contra locais de culto na Jordânia são incomuns. Em 2016, um ataque na cidade de Karak teve como alvos um centro de segurança e patrulhas policiais e deixou dez mortos.

Segundo o balanço mais recente das autoridades, nove pessoas morreram e 25 ficaram feridas no ataque contra cristãos do reino, cometido na sexta-feira por homens armados na aldeia de Hamud, no sul do país, durante uma procissão fúnebre.

A província de Karak, onde fica Hamud, abriga uma importante comunidade cristã no reino, de maioria muçulmana.

Os agressores invadiram o complexo da Igreja Greco-Ortodoxa de São Jorge antes de abrir fogo contra um cortejo fúnebre, segundo a polícia.

Os três suspeitos, classificados como "terroristas", foram detidos em uma casa abandonada na província de Karak, onde haviam se entrincheirado.

"Dois são irmãos e o terceiro é cunhado deles. Todos seguem a ideologia takfirista (islamismo extremista)", informou o diretor de Segurança Pública, Abdullah Maaytah, durante uma entrevista coletiva.

Segundo o responsável pela segurança, os suspeitos ficaram feridos durante as trocas de tiros com as forças de segurança no momento da prisão e foram hospitalizados. Armas e "uma grande quantidade de munição" foram apreendidas na residência, acrescentou.

"Prendemos os assassinos, estamos avaliando todas as circunstâncias que levam os jovens ao extremismo e responsabilizaremos todos aqueles cujo envolvimento for comprovado", afirmou o ministro do Interior, Mazen Al Faraya, na rede social X.

Segundo ele, "nada indica que eles tenham mantido contatos com o exterior ou colaborado com partes estrangeiras".

O rei Abdullah II, que se encontrou com vítimas após o ataque, afirmou no sábado, durante uma reunião do Conselho de Segurança Nacional, que "a segurança e a proteção dos jordanianos são uma linha vermelha que não deve ser ultrapassada".

O primeiro-ministro jordaniano, Jafar Hassan, decretou três dias de luto nacional a partir de sexta-feira, com bandeiras hasteadas a meio mastro em instituições governamentais e públicas.

articles.title: PM to inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3 online on Nov 3; 17 stations to open
articles.summary: PM Modi to virtually inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3 (Hinjewadi–Shivajinagar) on Nov 3; 17 of 23 stations cleared by CMRS to open for passengers.
articles.body: Pune: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will virtually inaugurate the Hinjewadi-Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 online on Nov 3, with chief minister Devendra Fadnavis attending the programme in the city, Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA) officials confirmed on Monday. Seventeen stations are expected to open for passenger services.Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA) commissioner Abhijit Chaudhari said, “We have been told to keep everything ready for Nov 3. PM will join online for the event, with chief minister and other dignitaries to be present at the venue.” Officials said the function will be held at Balewadi stadium. Mahametro will also have a ground breaking ceremony of their phase 2 here, officials added.The proposed launch comes after repeated delays. IT employees waiting for the metro to ease their daily commute to Hinjewadi’s IT parks had hoped Modi’s proposed Baramati visit would pave the way for the opening, but its postponement had raised fresh uncertainty over the launch.On Sunday, Shiv Sena (UBT) neta Aaditya Thackeray questioned why commuters should have to wait for a formal inauguration when the cleared stretch could be opened for public use. He urged state govt to start services for residents’ convenience and hold a grand inauguration later when PM was available. He also raised concerns over poor roads, traffic congestion and civic infrastructure in Hinjewadi.The 23.3km corridor has received commissioner of metro railway safety (CMRS) clearance for 17 of its 23 stations. Inspections of two more stations near Balewadi have been completed, with clearances expected shortly. Four stations — RBI, Simla Chowk, Mahabaleshwar Chowk and Baner — remain pending approval.Sachin Londhe, president of the Pimpri Chinchwad Cooperative Housing Societies Federation, said IT employees had been following up with PMRDA and metro authorities since July 2025 but had yet to receive a positive response to their concerns.“We launched the online Unclog Hinjawadi IT Park petition in June 2025, which garnered 39,000 signatures in 40 days. The Metro is a crucial public transport link that can ease congestion and improve connectivity for IT employees. Its inauguration at the earliest is important to encourage greater use of public transport,” Londhe said. He said IT employees had also worked with civic and police authorities to improve traffic movement in Hinjewadi following a meeting with the chief minister in July 2025.The corridor, being implemented by PMRDA through a public-private partnership, is expected to ease congestion between Hinjewadi and central Pune. articles.title: Rio Capivari volta subir, atinge 3,2 metros e mantém alerta para extravasamento; veja interdições | G1
articles.standfirst: Após chuvas de mais de 80 milímetros, manancial começou a baixar nesta segunda-feira (26), mas retomou patamar acima dos 3 metros nesta terça-feira (27).
articles.summary: Após chuvas de mais de 80 milímetros, manancial começou a baixar nesta segunda-feira (26), mas retomou patamar acima dos 3 metros nesta terça-feira (27).
articles.body:
O nível do Rio Capivari voltou a subir nesta terça-feira (27). Perto das 9h, o manancial registrava 3,20 metros, conforme última medição divulgada pela Defesa Civil, mantendo-se neste patamar até a publicação desta reportagem.

Apesar da estabilização, o rio permanece acima da cota de extravasamento, que é de 2,35 metros.

Capivari permancede em estado de alerta e a Defesa Civil continua monitorando o rio e as áreas de risco. A cidade mantém trechos interditados após as chuvas, de mais de 80 milímetros registradas entre o último domingo (25) e segunda-feira (26).

A coleta seletiva na cidade foi suspensa até 3 de novembro. - Entenda mais, abaixo.

"A elevação registrada nas últimas horas ocorreu devido à chegada das águas da região de Campinas. A estabilização não significa que o risco de alagamentos tenha cessado, e a população deve continuar respeitando as interdições e as orientações das equipes", detalhou a prefeitura de Capivari.

Rio Capivari transborda, atinge casas e provoca interdições em Capivari — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Na manhã da última segunda-feira (26), o nível do Rio Capivari tinha baixado para 2,4 metros. Nesta terça, voltou a superar os 3 metros.

A cidade registrou, pelo menos, dez pontos de alagamentos e ruas interditadas. Alguns deles já foram liberados. A prefeitura afirma que já começou os trabalhos de limpeza. Veja locais, abaixo.

A Prefeitura de Capivari divulgou os principais pontos de alagamentos e interdições às 8h30 desta terça-feira.

Rua Bento Dias com a Alameda Faustina Franchi Annicchino (Centro)

Avenida José Annicchino – Cortume (Centro)

Rua Emílio Alves Ferreira (Jardim Elisa)

Rua Antônio Pires com a Sete de Setembro (Centro)

A cota de extravasamento do Rio Capivari é de 2,35 metros. O manancial transborda ao ultrapassar essa marca.

Diante da situação, o município permanece em estado de alerta e monitora os bairros mais atingidos.

O bairro Moreto, especialmente a Rua João Moretti foi a mais atingida. "As equipes da Defesa Civil seguem monitorando o nível do rio e as áreas de risco, acompanhando a evolução do cenário e adotando as medidas necessárias para garantir a segurança da população", disse.

A Prefeitura de Capivari informou na manhã desta segunda-feira (26) que o serviço de Coleta Seletiva foi suspenso durante esta semana devido às enchentes.

"A medida foi necessária para que as equipes possam concentrar os trabalhos na limpeza das vias atingidas. A suspensão seguirá até segunda-feira, dia 2 de novembro, quando é celebrado o feriado nacional de Finados. Com isso, a Coleta Seletiva será retomada somente na terça-feira (3)", afirmou.

Durante esse período, a orientação é que os moradores mantenham os materiais recicláveis armazenados em locais adequados, evitando deixá-los nas calçadas e vias públicas até a retomada do serviço.

Rio Capivari começa a baixar depois de atingir três metros e transbordar em Capivari — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

"A Prefeitura agradece a compreensão e a colaboração da população e reforça que a suspensão é temporária, permitindo que as equipes priorizem os trabalhos de limpeza e recuperação das áreas afetadas pela enchente", completou.

A auxiliar de lavanderia, Selma dos Santos, registrou a hora em que o nível do rio começou a subir. Ela não conseguiu salvar muita coisa.

“Geladeira, sofá, rack, mesa, tudo. Só trouxe esse colchão. Agora, é esperar a água baixar para ver o que salvou, o que não salvou e seguir a vida", disse.

'Não acredito que vou ter que sair de casa'

A aposentada Aparecida Andrade também relatou momentos de angústia. "Aqui estava cheio de água", conta mostrando parte da casa. "Aí, vi os vizinhos chamando os vizinhos para levantar que a água tava subindo", lembrou.

A Aparecida foi uma das primeiras a deixar a casa em que mora. "Eu abri a janela, que eu olhei, o amigo já estava para o lado de fora. Meu Deus, eu não acredito que eu vou ter que sair", lamentou.

Na Rua Padre Arnaldo, a casa da Sueli Bergamini por pouco não foi atingida. "Erguemos tudo, só que a gente nunca teve ajuda de ninguém aqui. Sempre a gente se vira sozinho", criticou.

Na última quinta-feira (22), diante da previsão de fortes chuvas nas cabeceiras do Rio Capivari, a Defesa Civil solicitou à empresa Raízen a abertura total das comportas da Barragem Leopoldina.

A medida preventiva teve como objetivo facilitar o escoamento da água e reduzir possíveis impactos no município.

A orientação é que motoristas e pedestres respeitem as interdições e a sinalização das equipes, utilizem rotas alternativas e não tentem atravessar ruas alagadas ou locais com correnteza.

A Defesa Civil segue acompanhando a situação e continuará repassando orientações diretamente nos bairros e pelos canais oficiais da Prefeitura. A população, especialmente os moradores de áreas de risco, deve permanecer atenta às atualizações e seguir as recomendações das equipes que atuam nos locais.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelos números 199 e (19) 3492-3186.

A Guarda Civil atende pelo telefone 153 e pelo WhatsApp (19) 3491-1311, enquanto o Corpo de Bombeiros pode ser acionado pelo 193. Os serviços de emergência funcionam 24 horas por dia, todos os dias da semana.

articles.title: EisenHaus em Blumenau une chope, gastronomia e rock na cidade natal da Eisenbahn | G1
articles.standfirst: Bar reabre ao lado da fábrica da cervejaria com música, área ao ar livre e prato criado pelo chef Henrique Fogaça
articles.summary: Bar reabre ao lado da fábrica da cervejaria com música, área ao ar livre e prato criado pelo chef Henrique Fogaça
articles.body:
EisenHaus combina referências industriais e elementos ligados ao rock; espaço reabriu ao lado da fábrica da Eisenbahn, em Blumenau — Foto: Divulgação

Chope servido, petiscos nas mesas e rock ao vivo deram o tom da abertura da EisenHaus, antigo Bar Estação Eisenbahn, em Blumenau. O evento reuniu convidados, imprensa e criadores de conteúdo para apresentar o local, que volta a receber o público como uma opção para quem quer aproveitar a cultura cervejeira da cidade.

Instalado junto à fábrica, na Rua Bahia, a EisenHaus carrega referências que remetem tanto às origens quanto ao momento atual da Eisenbahn. A estética industrial se mistura a cores e elementos ligados ao rock, universo que ganhou espaço no posicionamento da cervejaria. Há um salão interno e uma ampla área externa, com mesas ao ar livre.

Da parte interna, é possível observar a estrutura da fábrica anexa. A área de produção não é aberta ao público, mas fica visível para quem está no bar e reforça a ligação entre os dois ambientes. Do lado de fora, outro detalhe remete ao passado: em frente ao local passava a antiga linha ferroviária que inspirou o nome Eisenbahn, palavra que significa “ferrovia” em alemão.

Fábrica da Eisenbahn segue em operação junto à EisenHaus, no mesmo endereço onde começou a história da cervejaria em Blumenau — Foto: Divulgação

A relação da cervejaria com Blumenau começou em 2002, quando os irmãos Juliano e Bruno Mendes criaram a Eisenbahn inspirados pela tradição cervejeira europeia. Mais de duas décadas depois, a reabertura do bar, fechado em 2020, recupera um ponto importante dessa trajetória justamente onde a produção permanece.

Para Juliano Mendes, cofundador da Eisenbahn, o retorno ganha outro significado depois do crescimento da cervejaria e da projeção conquistada dentro e fora do Brasil.

É um momento muito especial porque é um retorno à casa. Muita coisa aconteceu ao longo desses anos. A Eisenbahn ganhou muitos prêmios internacionais, cresceu no Brasil e ganhou projeção. Voltar e trazer toda essa história acumulada para a origem, para onde tudo começou, é muito especial para todos nós e para a cidade de Blumenau — afirma.

A proximidade entre o bar e a fábrica, segundo Juliano, é também uma forma de aproximar moradores e turistas do universo da Eisenbahn.

É um lugar onde os turistas e o próprio blumenauense podem viver essa experiência de estar em um bar bebendo cerveja com a produção acontecendo ao lado — completa.

A proposta também dialoga com a vocação cervejeira de Blumenau, destino que recebe visitantes atraídos por essa cultura, especialmente durante o mês de outubro. A intenção, porém, é manter a EisenHaus presente na rotina da cidade durante todo o ano.

A abertura ocorre justamente em um período de grande movimentação turística em Blumenau. Para a Eisenbahn, no entanto, a presença na cidade não se resume à temporada de outubro.

Renan Ciccone, diretor de Marketing do Grupo HEINEKEN Brasil, explica que a estratégia é fortalecer o vínculo com o lugar onde a Eisenbahn nasceu e manter essa presença independentemente dos grandes eventos.

A gente não enxerga isso como um desafio. Chegamos justamente neste mês para mostrar que viemos para ficar e, na verdade, sempre fomos daqui. É o que estamos dizendo hoje em Blumenau: tem cerveja que vem pra festa e tem cerveja que nasceu aqui — afirma.

Segundo Ciccone, a retomada do bar integra um movimento mais amplo de fortalecimento da Eisenbahn na região, que envolve também os estabelecimentos parceiros e a produção local.

O bar vai ficar. Vamos continuar investindo em Blumenau, obviamente também nos nossos bares parceiros. O intuito de voltar com o bar é retomar esse orgulho, mostrar para todo mundo que somos de Blumenau e que vamos continuar aqui em todas as épocas do ano e não só durante as festas — acrescenta.

A decisão de voltar em 2026 também acompanha a consolidação do posicionamento da Eisenbahn. Depois do fechamento do antigo bar, em 2020, e das transformações dos anos seguintes, a cervejaria passou a trabalhar de forma mais clara territórios ligados ao espírito empreendedor e a atitude locomotiva, além de estreitar sua relação com o rock por meio da plataforma Eisen Rock Station.

Essa identidade aparece na EisenHaus. Iluminação, cores, referências industriais e música compõem o local e levam para o ambiente físico elementos que hoje fazem parte da comunicação da Eisenbahn.

A agenda de atrações será divulgada pelos canais oficiais do EisenHaus .

A cozinha é outra parte importante da proposta. Além dos petiscos do cardápio, a EisenHaus conta com um prato criado por Henrique Fogaça, chef e embaixador da Eisenbahn.

Chef e embaixador da Eisenbahn, Henrique Fogaça participou da abertura da EisenHaus e apresentou o prato criado especialmente para o bar — Foto: Divulgação

A receita tem como protagonista a costela bovina, preparada com especiarias e cerveja. A carne é cozida, desfiada e finalizada com o caldo do próprio preparo, que passa por uma redução para concentrar os sabores.

Segundo Fogaça, um dos principais cuidados na criação foi encontrar o equilíbrio entre os ingredientes e a bebida utilizada na receita.

O maior desafio foi achar o ponto ideal para que a cerveja desse continuidade aos sabores e não interferisse em nada. Estamos em Blumenau, na terra da cerveja, então nada mais justo do que pensar o prato dessa forma — explica.

Cremosidade, picância e personalidade são algumas das características destacadas pelo chef. Para ele, a comida também pode se tornar parte da lembrança de quem passa pela cidade.

Espero que as pessoas tenham uma experiência que fique guardada na memória. Que pensem: “Fui para Blumenau, conheci a EisenHaus, experimentei o prato do Fogaça”. É criar uma memória afetiva através da comida — diz.

Prato criado pelo chef Henrique Fogaça para a EisenHaus tem costela bovina preparada com especiarias e cerveja entre os ingredientes — Foto: Divulgação

A relação de Fogaça com a Eisenbahn começou antes mesmo de ele se tornar embaixador. Durante a abertura, o chef relembrou rótulos que consumia anos atrás e a proximidade que já tinha com a cervejaria antes da parceria profissional.

Cerveja, gastronomia, música e a ligação com o lugar onde a Eisenbahn nasceu formam a proposta da EisenHaus. Para os moradores, o bar representa a retomada de um ponto que fez parte da trajetória da cervejaria. Para os turistas, acrescenta uma parada ao roteiro de quem chega a Blumenau atraído pela cultura cervejeira.

articles.title: Virada inédita de Lula nas urnas é impulsionada por dois fatores: ruas e redes | G1
articles.standfirst: O deputado federal André Janones, da Rede, assumiu o papel de estrategista digital. Foi dele a ideia de criar o canal 'Exército do Lula' no WhatsApp.
articles.summary: O deputado federal André Janones, da Rede, assumiu o papel de estrategista digital. Foi dele a ideia de criar o canal 'Exército do Lula' no WhatsApp.
articles.body:
A virada inédita nas urnas foi impulsionada por dois fatores: ruas e redes. Foi essa a estratégia da campanha de Lula depois de sair atrás no primeiro turno.

“Há muitos anos, não tinham visto uma movimentação da sociedade como nós temos visto nesse segundo turno", disse Lula em 24 de outubro de 2024.

O combustível da virada foi o susto nas urnas. No primeiro turno, Flávio Bolsonaro terminou na frente. Lula admitiu a surpresa e avisou que começava ali uma nova eleição:

“O resultado muitas vezes é inesperado. Eu confesso para vocês que eu estava convencido que eu ia ganhar as eleições no primeiro turno".

O resultado provocou uma reação imediata, que começou em grupos de mensagens e ganhou as ruas . Logo após o primeiro turno, estudantes da Universidade Federal Fluminense, em Niterói, organizaram o primeiro ato de rua da nova fase da disputa - que foi seguido por outros tantos.

Virada inédita de Lula nas urnas é impulsionada por dois fatores: ruas e redes — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A campanha montou um quartel-general em Brasília e criou uma força-tarefa digital. O núcleo reuniu jovens deputados recém-eleitos, como Jones Manoel e Guilherme Cortez, do PSOL, e Ana Júlia Ribeiro, do PT - todos com votações expressivas, para acertar a rota. A missão era transformar a frustração em engajamento rápido, como lembra a deputada federal Ana Elisa, do PT, que também integrou o grupo:

“As percepções das pessoas mudam no dia a dia. Hoje, com acesso exacerbado às redes sociais, as percepções das pessoas, os votos das pessoas viram a cada dia. Então, eu realmente acreditava na virada, mas eu não pensava que seria dessa forma estrondosa".

O deputado federal André Janones, da Rede, assumiu o papel de estrategista digital. Foi dele a ideia de criar o canal "Exército do Lula" no WhatsApp. O grupo foi ganhando força, multiplicando as adesões e chegou a mais de 10,5 milhões de inscritos na reta final.

“A analogia que eu fiz: o Messi nunca deixou de ser gênio. Ele não deixa de ser gênio quando ele fala para a seleção da Argentina: ‘Olha, eu não consigo correr mais. Corram por mim que o restante eu faço’. Os jovens disseram: ‘Eu corro por você’. É exatamente o que nós fizemos pelo Lula", afirmou André Janones.

As manifestações de rua cresceram pelo Brasil. E o trabalho de formiguinha foi ganhando adeptos e força. João Ricardo Dias é advogado no Rio de Janeiro. Nas últimas semanas, foi para as ruas conversar e convencer eleitores:

“Realmente eu sinto que a minha mobilização, ela não, não é só minha. Assim, é representativo de uma geração toda que estava aí disposta para lutar por um projeto que faça o país perseverar aí pelos próximos quatro anos".

Enquanto a militância agia nas ruas, a campanha consolidava os papéis do vice Geraldo Alckmin, que reforçou a estabilidade, e dos ex-ministros Fernando Haddad, Simone Tebet e Marina Silva. Esse esforço contou com a atuação do ministro Camilo Santana e de governadores, como Rafael Fonteles, do PT - reeleito com mais de 70% dos votos no Piauí -, que entrou para a coordenação da campanha na reta final. Em entrevista ao Estúdio i, na GloboNews, Fonteles comentou a aproximação de Lula com as redes sociais:

“Ele passou a usar mais enfaticamente, mais frequentemente, as redes sociais. E também as ruas se levantaram mais, os jovens, a população em geral. E uma coisa alimenta a outra. As redes sociais alimentam as ruas, as ruas alimentam as redes".

A campanha também mirou nos eleitores que não tinham votado no primeiro turno. Foram mais de 33 milhões de brasileiros. Os mais velhos responderam à convocação. E foi exatamente a união desses dois mundos - a guerrilha de mensagens nas redes sociais e a presença maciça nas ruas em diferentes pontos do país - que impulsionou a virada nas urnas. Assim que o resultado oficial foi confirmado, a energia das ruas se transformou em celebração. Para quem mergulhou na campanha, a tensão dos últimos dias deu lugar ao alívio da vitória.

articles.summary: O processo seletivo do Samu na Zona da Mata oferece vagas para médicos, técnicos e condutores com inscrições gratuitas pela internet até quarta-feira (28).
articles.body:
Termina, nesta quarta-feira (28), o prazo para inscrições do processo seletivo que oferece sete vagas temporárias para preenchimento imediato e formação de cadastro de reserva para o Consórcio Intermunicipal de Saúde da Rede de Urgência do Sudeste de Minas Gerais (Cisdeste). Os salários chegam a R$ 8.899,89, de acordo com o cargo pretendido.

As vagas são para condutor socorrista , cargo que exige ensino médio e carteira nacional de habilitação D; técnico de enfermagem , para candidatos com habilitação na área; e médico , para graduados que tenham registro no Conselho Regional de Medicina. Os profissionais irão atuar no Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu 192).

As oportunidades estão distribuídas entre as cidades de Juiz de Fora , Alvinópolis, Bom Jardim de Minas , Carangola , Cataguases , Divino , Ervália , Laranjal , Leopoldina , Mercês , Ponte Nova, Rio Pomba , Senador Firmino e Visconde do Rio Branco .

Samu Cisdeste Juiz de Fora — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

As inscrições são gratuitas e devem ser feitas pela internet, por meio dos formulários indicados no edital da seleção . Os interessados devem preencher o formulário correspondente ao cargo pretendido, indicar a base de interesse e anexar a documentação necessária.

O edital reúne os requisitos para cada função, a remuneração, a jornada de trabalho, os documentos exigidos e as condições dos contratos temporários .

O processo seletivo será feito por análise de títulos, considerando critérios de formação e experiência profissional . O resultado será divulgado no site do Cideste .

articles.title: Colorado family’s farm grew from 160 to 10,000 acres over more than a century; about 30 wind turbines were expected to bring in at least $180,000 a year
articles.summary: A family farm in eastern Colorado grew from 160 acres to 10,000 acres over more than a century.
articles.body: A family farm in eastern Colorado grew from 160 acres to 10,000 acres over more than a century. Around 30 wind turbines on the property were expected to generate at least $180,000 a year for the family, providing a steady source of income alongside farming. Andrew and Lucy Kochis moved from what is now Slovakia to Colorado in 1908 under the Homestead Act.Four generations later, Jan and Virgil Kochis continued farming in Matheson, where limited rainfall made crop production unpredictable. According to KUNC, the turbines were part of Xcel Energy’s Rush Creek wind farm. Their payments were expected to provide income even during droughts and hailstorms, while crops and cattle continued to grow beneath them.How the Kochis family established its Colorado farm in 1908Andrew and Lucy Kochis arrived in Colorado in 1908 with their four surviving children after moving from what is now Slovakia to the United States. They had worked in coal mines in Pennsylvania and Indiana and had lost a three-month-old baby. The Homestead Act gave them a chance to own land if they made it productive within five years.The family received 160 acres on the eastern plains and built a one-room house from clay bricks with a grass-covered roof. In 1914, they secured the title to the land. Their farm later received recognition as a Colorado Centennial Farm, an honour held by about 1,800 farms across the Mountain West region, according to the report.Dry conditions made farming difficult for the Kochis familyFarming on the eastern Colorado plains depended on rainfall. The Kochises grew crops without irrigation because water was either unavailable or too deep to reach. Their farm faced unpredictable rainfall, changing wheat prices, and crop challenges. The family tried growing sunflowers but stopped because the plants used too much water.They also switched among wheat, milo, corn, and wheat seed to improve their chances of producing a crop in changing weather conditions. Work outside the farm helped supplement uncertain earnings. The family kept off-farm jobs in coal mining, highway construction, and school bus driving, while Jan Kochis worked part-time as a nutritionist. Dry conditions continued to cause difficulties.Around 30 wind turbines joined the 10,000-acre Colorado farmBy 2018, the Kochis farm had expanded from its original 160 acres to 10,000 acres. About 30 turbines had already been built on Jan and Virgil Kochis’s property. Xcel, Colorado’s largest utility company, was expected to complete the state’s largest wind farm within the following few months. The wider project was planned to cover 95,000 acres across four Colorado counties. From outside their home, the couple could see the installed turbines stretching across the farm’s fields. The structures stood about 30 storeys tall and had long grey blades. Cows were already gathering in the shade beneath one turbine.Wind turbines were expected to bring in at least $180,000 annuallyThe turbines were expected to provide the family with a steadier income than crops alone could generate. Under the arrangement described in 2018, the Kochises were due to receive a minimum of about $6,000 per turbine each year for the next few decades, with higher payments expected once the turbines began producing electricity.With around 30 turbines on their property, the minimum annual payment was expected to reach at least $180,000. KUNC reported that this amount would equal about a 60% increase on the farm’s gross income in a good year. The payments were expected to continue whether the farm faced hail or drought, while crops and cattle could still grow beneath the turbines. articles.body: AMRITSAR: The son of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch was shot dead and his friend was injured when assailants opened fire on them outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village, falling under Chatiwind police station, on Monday evening.The victim, Teerath Singh, was returning after paying obeisance at the gurdwara along with his friend Ranjit Singh when the assailants allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving both injured.Teerath was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead, officials said.Yadwinder Singh, Deputy superintendent of police (DSP), Attari, said that Ranjit, who sustained a bullet injury, is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.The preliminary investigations suggested that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.He further said police have identified four persons, Gurditt Singh, Gurjant Singh, Harkirat Singh alias Hockey, and Gora, and registered an FIR naming them, but no arrests have been made so far.The DSP said that teams have been constituted to investigate the case and arrest the accused.Police sources also informed that the family of Teerath also suspects the involvement of a rival group from the village behind the incident.Notably, Teerath’s brother Karaj Singh had won the sarpanch election on an AAP ticket.The killing triggered a political attack on the AAP government, with former union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu questioning its ability to maintain law and order in Punjab.In a X post, he said, “The murder of Teerath Singh, brother of an incumbent AAP sarpanch, outside a gurdwara in Amritsar is a stark indictment of Punjab’s collapsed law and order. articles.title: That ruby may be more than what meets the eye: Expert shares 5 things to check before buying a gemstone
articles.summary: A gemstone can spend millions of years forming beneath the Earth's surface, only to be chosen in a few minutes because its colour catches someone's eye.
articles.body: A gemstone can spend millions of years forming beneath the Earth's surface, only to be chosen in a few minutes because its colour catches someone's eye. But that brilliant ruby, deep blue sapphire or vivid emerald may have a story that goes far beyond its appearance. Was it formed naturally or grown in a laboratory? Has it been treated to improve its colour? Can a certificate establish what it really is? And if you're buying it for astrological reasons, what should you know before wearing it?For centuries, coloured gemstones have occupied a fascinating space between nature, craftsmanship, personal taste and belief. They have adorned royal jewellery, travelled through generations as family heirlooms and become part of traditions surrounding marriage, prosperity and astrology. Yet choosing one involves more than finding a stone that looks beautiful.For Diya Jagasia, founder of Cosmic Gemstones, the decision begins with understanding why a person wants a gemstone in the first place. Someone buying an emerald for its rich green colour may have very different priorities from someone seeking a stone for its place in Vedic astrological traditions.Jagasia is drawn to this intersection of beauty, nature and astrology. She even hopes to spend her seventies studying gemstones from a mountain villa. Until then, her advice for anyone considering a purchase is practical: understand what you're buying, ask the right questions and give yourself time to choose.Here are five things she believes every buyer should consider.1. Buying a gemstone for astrology? Start with the recommendation, not the stoneA gemstone may catch your eye in a shop window, but if you're buying it for astrological reasons, Jagasia advises against choosing one simply because a friend wears it or a relative recommends it.Within Vedic astrology, different gemstones are associated with particular planets and astrological interpretations. Practitioners may recommend stones after examining an individual's birth chart. If you follow these traditions, seek guidance from a practitioner you trust rather than assuming that a gemstone considered auspicious for one person will be suitable for everyone.Jagasia compares this approach to understanding individual needs before making a choice. Her point is that a recommendation should be personal, not based on a passing trend or someone else's experience.It is worth distinguishing traditional belief from established science, however. There is no robust scientific evidence that gemstones can alter planetary influences or reliably change a person's fortune. Buyers can still value their cultural or spiritual significance while making an informed decision about what they purchase.2. The jeweller matters as much as the gemstoneA beautiful stone can be difficult for an inexperienced buyer to assess. Colour alone cannot establish its identity, origin, treatment history or value. That is where the jeweller becomes important.In many Indian families, jewellery buying is built on relationships. People return to the same jeweller their parents or grandparents trusted, relying on years of familiarity and word of mouth. That continuity can be useful, but it should not replace asking questions.Look for a seller who can explain the gemstone's characteristics, disclose known treatments, provide appropriate documentation and clearly state what you are paying for. Ask about the return policy, too, particularly when buying a valuable stone.A trustworthy jeweller should be willing to explain the details without pressuring you into a purchase. If basic questions about whether a stone is natural, treated or lab-grown are met with vague answers, take your time before committing.3. Natural, treated or lab-grown: Know the differenceTwo gemstones can look remarkably similar while having different origins and histories. Understanding those differences is one of the most important steps before buying. Natural gemstones form through geological processes within the Earth over long periods.Treated gemstones are natural stones that have undergone processes intended to improve their appearance or other characteristics. Treatments vary by gemstone and may include heating, irradiation or fracture filling. Some are widely accepted in the trade, but they can affect a stone's value and must be disclosed appropriately.Lab-grown gemstones are created through controlled processes that reproduce many of the conditions involved in natural gemstone formation. They can share the same chemical composition and crystal structure as their natural counterparts, although they have different origins. They are not necessarily imitations: an imitation merely resembles another gemstone, while a lab-grown stone may be the same gemstone material produced artificially.These distinctions matter when comparing prices, assessing resale expectations or buying a stone for a particular purpose.Jagasia notes that people buying gemstones for Vedic astrological practices may specifically seek natural, untreated stones because of traditional beliefs about their significance. That is a matter of belief rather than a scientifically established property of the stones.For buyers primarily interested in colour, design and wearability, treated or lab-grown options may also be worth considering. The important thing is to know exactly what you are buying and whether it matches your expectations.4. A gemstone certificate is more than a piece of paperworkA stone may look impressive under shop lighting, but appearance alone cannot tell you everything about it. A report from a reputable gemmological laboratory can help establish its identity and disclose detectable treatments or whether it is natural or laboratory-grown.Before purchasing an expensive gemstone, ask what documentation is available and check which laboratory issued the report. Make sure the report corresponds to the stone being sold to you. Where possible, verify the report directly with the issuing laboratory.It is also important to understand what the document does not establish. A gemstone identification report is not automatically a valuation certificate, a guarantee of future resale value or proof of every claim a seller might make about the stone.Jagasia compares a gemstone report to an Aadhaar card: a useful form of identification that should be kept safely. The analogy has its limits, but the underlying advice is sound. Retain the report, purchase invoice and any treatment disclosures, particularly if you intend to insure the jewellery, resell it or pass it down as a family heirloom.5. The most beautiful gemstone is the one you will actually wearThere is a temptation to equate a gemstone's worth with its size, rarity or price. But a large statement stone that rarely leaves its box may bring less personal satisfaction than a smaller one that becomes part of your everyday jewellery.Think about how you intend to wear it. Will it be set in a ring, pendant or pair of earrings? Does the design suit your lifestyle? Will the setting protect the stone adequately?If the stone carries spiritual or astrological meaning for you, wearing it may also become a personal ritual. If you are drawn to gemstones for their colour or craftsmanship, that connection can be just as meaningful in its own way.Jagasia's advice is to choose something you genuinely enjoy wearing rather than buying a stone simply because it is fashionable, expensive or recommended by someone else.A purchase worth taking your time overColoured gemstones are unusual objects: they bring together geological history, human craftsmanship, cultural traditions and individual taste. Their appeal can lie in a rare colour, a family story, a long-standing belief or the simple pleasure of finding a stone that feels unmistakably yours.That personal connection need not come at the expense of practical judgement. Ask questions about origin and treatment, seek independent documentation when appropriate, understand the limits of astrological claims and never feel pressured to buy before you are ready.The biggest or most expensive gemstone is not automatically the right choice. A well-informed purchase begins with knowing what matters to you, what the stone can genuinely offer and what you are paying for.Choose with curiosity, buy with clarity and let the meaning of the gemstone be your own.You use AI every day. articles.body: In June, 2008, 44 retired New York City subway cars were submerged into the Atlantic Ocean off Virginia’s Eastern Shore. With this, the subway cars began a new chapter as part of an artificial fishing reef. The Virginia Marine Resources Commission (VMRC) carried out the deployment near Chincoteague in an operation that carried on for the whole day, designed to expand Blackfish Bank Reef. New York’s Metropolitan Transit Authority had donated the stainless-steel cars, and they were placed in a grid pattern on the seabed. The commission reported that each car measured 50 feet and that the cars weighed 17 tons combined. Instead of creating a new reef, the operation expanded an established site that already contained retired subway cars and surplus military vehicles.From New York’s subway system to Virginia’s seabedThe cars initially served New York City’s public transport network. Following retirement, they were repurposed as artificial reef material, adding physical structures to the underwater environment. The VMRC reported that such materials provide shelter for marine species and can help support a food web that attracts larger predatory fish. The agency presented the deployment as a method to expand habitat and recreational fishing opportunities, not as proof that fish populations had already increased as a result of the new structures.The Blackfish Bank Reef lies 5.8 nautical miles southeast of Assateague Island, Maryland, off the coast of Chincoteague, Virginia. The deployment in 2008 was the third major addition to the site documented in the commission’s announcement. In 1998, 40 surplus Army armoured personnel carriers had been lowered there. 50 retired New York City “Redbird” subway cars followed in November 2003.Together, the three deployments account for 134 vehicles: 94 subway cars and 40 armoured personnel carriers. They were installed in separate operations over a decade, and the 17-ton figure refers to the combined reported weight of the 44 cars deployed in 2008.How artificial reefs create underwater habitatArtificial reefs are formed by placing suitable structures on the seabed to provide additional physical support and surfaces that marine organisms can colonise. These structures can create shelter for invertebrates and fish depending on the material, location and environmental conditions. Additionally, the organisms living on or around the structure can become a part of the local food web. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection describes artificial reefs as structures that provide habitat on otherwise sandy seabeds and attract marine organisms and fish.Meanwhile, for Blackfish Bank, the immediate purpose of the 2008 operation was to expand the existing fishing reef. According to the VMRC, the submerged cars have been deployed as structures that could attract gamefish, thus making the site more useful for recreational anglers.Part of Virginia’s wider artificial reef programmeThe subway-car deployment formed part of a programme that the VMRC had been developing since the early 1970s. By June 2008, the agency reported maintaining 23 artificial reefs throughout Chesapeake Bay and coastal waters of Virginia. These sites used a range of materials, including old concrete pipes, demolished bridge sections, pier remains, a lighthouse, subway cars, armoured personnel carriers and retired ships. Therefore, the project extended beyond one unusual deployment, using different structures to create habitats underwater at several locations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Meet Bethany: The 15-year-old student whose portrait of a school storyteller led to a published book illustration career and helped her build confidence despite situational mutism
articles.summary: A 15-year-old student from Cambridgeshire has become a published book illustrator after a portrait she drew during a school storytelling session caught an
articles.body: A 15-year-old student from Cambridgeshire has become a published book illustrator after a portrait she drew during a school storytelling session caught an author's attention. Bethany, who experiences situational mutism, was sketching Chip Colquhoun to help her concentrate when he noticed her artwork and later invited her to illustrate his children's book. As reported by the BBC, the experience has helped her build confidence, attend book launches and take part in radio interviews, although she continues to need support in unfamiliar situations. Bethany is now working on illustrations for another book while balancing her creative projects with schoolwork.How a school portrait helped Bethany become a published book illustratorThe opportunity began when storyteller and author Chip Colquhoun visited Bethany's school to lead a storytelling session. Sitting among the audience, Bethany started drawing a portrait of him. She was using the activity to help herself concentrate, rather than setting out to attract the attention of the visitor.Colquhoun noticed the finished drawing and was impressed enough to approach her about illustrating one of his books. Bethany's portrait later appeared in a book offering educators advice on using storytelling as a teaching tool. The encounter also led to a larger commission: illustrating The Bestest Story in the World Ever!, which was published in September 2026.For Bethany, seeing her work reproduced in a book was an unfamiliar experience. Speaking to BBC Radio Cambridgeshire's Louise Hulland, she described the feeling as ‘really weird and surreal’.She also looked back at the portrait that had started the process with a degree of distance. Her style has changed since then, she explained, and she considers the drawing different from the way she works now. Even so, she felt it was a good effort for the level of skill she had at the time. Colquhoun said the portrait had caught his attention from the outset."Drawing at that point helped me focus, so I needed something to draw and he was right there”, Bethany said.Daily challenges Bethany faces with situational mutismBethany's growing experience as an illustrator has taken place alongside the difficulties she faces with communication.She explained that she can speak to some people but may be unable to talk to others, particularly when she does not know them or feels uncomfortable around them.Her mother, Fiona, said Bethany developed language normally as a child. The difficulty is not a lack of language ability, but the circumstances in which she can use it. "It comes from a place of severe anxiety which almost paralyses her and she is unable to talk.”Situational mutism, also known as selective mutism, is associated with severe anxiety that can prevent a person from speaking in particular settings.Fiona described how the condition can leave her daughter unable to respond verbally even when she knows what she wants to say. "When she is in familiar surroundings or with familiar and trusted people she is able to use her language skills - but not always."The effects extend beyond individual conversations. According to Fiona, Bethany is still unable to go out on her own beyond the home or school. Everyday activities that other teenagers might manage independently can therefore require support.Bethany gains confidence through her book illustration workBethany said, "If I was here a few years ago, I wouldn't be doing this because I would be too nervous and I would be too stressed." She has found herself doing things that she would previously have avoided because of the anxiety involved.Her progress has not meant that the difficulties have disappeared, but she has been able to approach some of these experiences with help from people around her. As reported by the BBC, Fiona said her daughter had attended two book launches and been interviewed by two radio stations. These were significant changes for a teenager who continues to need support when facing situations outside her usual surroundings.Bethany's work has also attracted praise from other illustrators, according to Colquhoun. The recognition has come through her drawings, giving her a way to share her abilities even when speaking remains difficult.Fiona said the important difference was that Bethany now had opportunities to feel proud of what she had achieved. Her daughter still could not manage these events independently, she explained, but she had wanted to try them when given support.More illustrations alongside schoolworkBethany has continued to develop her portfolio since completing the illustrations for The Bestest Story in the World Ever!. She is now working on a third book and has three drawings to complete for another project. She told BBC Radio Cambridgeshire that she usually draws at around 8pm or 9pm. That routine allows her to keep up with her studies while making progress on the projects she has taken on. She continues to live with the challenges of situational mutism, but illustration has become a way for her to take part in projects beyond the classroom and share her work with a wider audience.You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Cars set ablaze, police motorcycle torched as violence rocks Spain's Bilbao
articles.summary: Nine people have been arrested in Bilbao, Spain, after violent clashes broke out following protests against a planned appearance by far-right activist
articles.body: Nine people have been arrested in Bilbao, Spain, after violent clashes broke out following protests against a planned appearance by far-right activist Vito Quiles. Fires engulfed cars and rubbish containers as riot police confronted demonstrators in the Deusto neighbourhood after the event was cancelled over security concerns.The Bilbao clashes occurred amid wider protests across Spain over housing affordability and the rising cost of living. The latest nationwide housing demonstrations began in late September following the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her Madrid home on September 23. The case drew public attention to rising rents, evictions and a shortage of affordable housing.Video footage circulating on social media on Monday showed hooded protesters moving through the streets, fires burning and barricades blocking roads. At least six cars, several rubbish containers and a municipal police motorcycle were damaged, while firefighters responded to multiple blazes. According to Spanish newspaper El Constitucional, the Basque government’s security department provided the provisional arrest count. The unrest erupted on Monday after earlier demonstrations against Quiles’ scheduled 7 pm appearance near the University of Deusto.Authorities said a group moved towards the Deusto police station, throwing stones and setting fire to the municipal police motorcycle. The security department alleged that those involved deliberately sought to cause disturbances despite knowing that the event had been cancelled.Quiles announced the cancellation in a post on X, saying he had spoken to the head of the police operation, who warned of a “very high” risk of incidents.In the same post, he accused protesters of being “former ETA members, street terrorists, and other criminals”, without providing evidence for the allegations. He also called demonstrators “scum” and said: “We will return to Bilbao. But after responding to them on 29N as they deserve.”Earlier, Quiles had described the response to his planned visit as “an unprecedented success”, claiming the mobilisation had brought “a lot of lazy people out of bed”.Protests began in the morning, when thousands of students marched through central Bilbao in a demonstration organised by Ikasle Antolakunde Sozialista (IAS). A second mobilisation took place in the afternoon, with demonstrators opposing what organisers described as the normalisation of sexist, racist and classist discourse.The University of Deusto suspended activities from 2 pm (local time) and closed its campus preventively at 3 pm (local time), following police instructions. The institution said the event had been organised externally, had not been authorised on campus and was not supported by the university.Wider tensions and investigationOn September 26, around 25,000 people protested in Madrid, according to the regional government delegation, while demonstrations and protest camps spread to other cities. The protests intensified on October 2, when parliament rejected two emergency housing decrees proposed by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s government. The measures included stronger protections against evictions and tighter rules on rentals. On October 3, demonstrations took place in around 50 cities, with protesters demanding affordable housing and greater tenant protection.Separately, authorities have raised concerns about extremist online messages allegedly encouraging attacks on police and crowds during demonstrations, Euronews reported, citing El País.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ed Sheeran performed at a private New York fundraiser for children in his home county of Suffolk; the evening raised $1 million to support local charities helping disadvantaged young people
articles.summary: A private fundraising evening in New York has brought a $1 million boost to charities supporting disadvantaged children and young people in Suffolk,
articles.body: A private fundraising evening in New York has brought a $1 million boost to charities supporting disadvantaged children and young people in Suffolk, England. Singer Ed Sheeran joined Ipswich Town Football Club chairman and chief executive Mark Ashton at the invitation-only event in late September 2026, where an exclusive performance and charity auction helped raise the money. According to the Lentonbrook Foundation’s official announcement, published on October 19, the entire amount will remain in Suffolk and support local charities and community organisations. The fundraising milestone will allow the foundation to expand its work with young people and families who need additional support.Ed Sheeran joins New York fundraising eventThe event brought together investors associated with Ipswich Town Football Club and guests from their wider networks. Former Ipswich Town captain Matt Holland hosted the evening, which featured a conversation with Ashton and Sheeran before the singer performed for attendees. A charity auction also formed part of the programme, helping the Lentonbrook Foundation raise $1 million, equivalent to approximately £750,000.The fundraiser was organised to support disadvantaged children and young people in Suffolk, Sheeran’s home county. Although the event took place thousands of miles away in New York, its proceeds are intended to benefit communities across the English county. Ashton, who founded the Lentonbrook Foundation, thanked Sheeran, the guests and everyone who contributed to the fundraising effort. He said the achievement would bring significant new funding to Suffolk and help local organisations reach more young people, create opportunities and make a lasting difference. The foundation said the money would build on its existing work with grassroots charities and community groups rather than support a single project.Foundation focuses on disadvantaged young peopleThe Lentonbrook Foundation was established by Ashton, who also serves as chairman and chief executive of Ipswich Town Football Club. Its work centres on supporting charities and community organisations that help underprivileged children and young people across Suffolk. The foundation supports a range of initiatives for disadvantaged children and young people, including projects that provide supportive environments, educational and recreational opportunities, and specialist services for vulnerable groups.Its existing projects demonstrate the range of support it provides. These include creating a sensory room at Langer Primary Academy in Felixstowe, funding youth activities delivered by Whitton Youth Partnership in Ipswich and supporting woodland adventure days through Green Light Trust. The foundation has also supported specialist services for young people affected by domestic abuse in West Suffolk.These initiatives address different challenges faced by children and families, from the need for supportive learning environments to access to outdoor experiences and services designed for vulnerable young people. The newly raised funds will enable the foundation to extend this work and provide additional assistance to organisations already connected to local communities.$1 million to remain in SuffolkOne of the central commitments attached to the fundraiser is that all the money raised will stay in Suffolk and directly benefit communities across the county. The foundation said local charities and community organisations were well placed to understand the needs of the children and families they serve. Additional funding could help these groups expand their services, reach more young people and provide opportunities that might otherwise be unavailable.For small community organisations, funding can support practical initiatives that make a difference to everyday life. These may include safe spaces for young people, activities outside school, access to specialist services and opportunities to participate in educational or recreational programmes. Ashton said the foundation wanted to help children access support and experiences they might otherwise miss. He described the fundraising result as an example of what could be achieved when people came together around a shared purpose. The Lentonbrook Foundation says it welcomes grant applications from charities and organisations supporting disadvantaged children and young people across Suffolk.Music and philanthropy support local communitiesSheeran’s appearance gave the private event a musical centrepiece, while the auction and contributions from attendees helped turn the evening into a significant fundraising effort. The result also reflects the role that private donors, business networks and public figures can play in supporting community organisations. By directing the proceeds towards existing local initiatives, the foundation intends to build on programmes that already have connections with children and families in need.The $1 million raised in New York will provide additional resources for charities working across Suffolk, from Ipswich and Felixstowe to communities in West Suffolk. For the Lentonbrook Foundation, the event represents a substantial fundraising milestone and an opportunity to broaden its support. For the organisations receiving assistance, the money could help extend services and create further opportunities for disadvantaged young people.The fundraiser's significance ultimately lies in its local impact. With all the money dedicated to Suffolk, the Lentonbrook Foundation aims to turn one evening of music, generosity and charitable giving into practical support for children and families across Sheeran’s home county.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2017, South Carolina sent a 168-foot bridge that carried traffic since 1939, 50 miles offshore; the reef drew grouper and billfish to a once-sandy seafloor
articles.summary: In 2017, South Carolina transformed a historic 168-foot bridge into a thriving artificial reef 50 miles off the Charleston coast, enhancing marine biodiversity and attracting grouper, billfish, and recreational anglers. Discover the journey from bridge to seabed and its benefits for marine life.
articles.body: Bridges do not last forever, and many are eventually sent for scrap. South Carolina chose a different fate for an old Highway 41 bridge in 2017. After carrying traffic over the Wando River near Charleston since 1939, the steel span was repurposed as part of an offshore artificial reef, where it provides habitat for marine life. The steel swing bridge once connected Mount Pleasant with the area near the Francis Marion National Forest across the Wando River. It measured 168 feet (about 51 metres) in length. After the replacement bridge opened, the old span was cleaned and attached to a retired barge. The combined structure was taken about 50 miles (80 kilometres) off Charleston and deployed in more than 300 feet (91 metres) of water as part of the South Carolina Memorial Reef. It was placed on the seabed rather than buried beneath sediment, adding hard structure and habitat to a previously sandy stretch of ocean floor.From highway to seabedIn August 2017, the old bridge was removed as vehicles began using the replacement span nearby. Crews lowered the old structure by crane onto a barge and cleaned it to remove materials that could harm the marine environment. The bridge was then secured to a retired barge measuring 130 feet long. The combined structure was deployed at the Charleston Deep Reef in October 2017, providing 44 feet of vertical relief above the seabed.The project required substantial funding as well as engineering work. The South Carolina Department of Natural Resources estimated the cost of purchasing, cleaning and transporting the structure at $180,000, with contributions expected from conservation groups and private donors. The Memorial Reef fund was established by independent anglers seeking to honour family members and friends through artificial reef projects. The South Carolina Governor’s Cup Advisory Board worked with the department to support the initiative. The project is located within the Charleston Deep Reef, a permitted marine protected area that Marlin magazine reported was established in 2009 before reef material was placed there.Grouper and billfishThe first structures went down in 2014. They were two retired barges piled high with shipping containers, truck chassis and radio towers. By the time the bridge came out in 2017, the department said, those barges were already doing well at attracting snowy grouper along with big billfish such as blue marlin and sailfish. The tournament coordinator for the Governor’s Cup Billfishing Series said the number of billfish caught and released in and around the reef that summer had been unlike anything seen before, and she expected the bridge to make the area livelier still. Robert Martore, the department’s artificial reef coordinator, said the earlier barges had worked so well for deepwater grouper that extra material could only add to the area’s productivity.The bridge and its barge were deliberately deployed on the Charleston Deep Reef in October 2017. The department's 2018 annual report lists the 168-foot bridge and the 130-foot barge among the structures placed on the reef. The same report records 17 reef construction projects at 15 sites that added more than 300,000 cubic feet of hard bottom habitat to South Carolina's offshore reefs during the fiscal year. It also reports that acoustic receivers detected highly migratory species passing through the reef areas at particular times of year, including animals from as far away as Massachusetts and Florida, as well as local migrants such as sturgeon and sea turtlesReports on the Charleston Deep Reef have documented deepwater snapper and grouper around its structures, alongside billfish that attract anglers to the area. The permitted reef site was intended to provide additional habitat for vulnerable snapper and grouper species while supporting offshore fishing opportunities.Why states sink old structuresArtificial reefs serve a similar function in the temperate waters off South Carolina, where tropical coral reefs do not naturally form. The South Carolina Department of Natural Resources says artificial reefs are usually placed on seabeds with little natural relief. These structures provide habitat, shelter and spawning grounds for fish while attracting recreational divers and anglers. For nearly four decades, the state has built artificial reefs using a range of retired structures, including bridge spans, military vehicles and subway cars.There is also an environmental argument. Old material used as habitat keeps it out of landfills, though anything meant for a reef has to go through a long and thorough cleaning procedure before it’s sunk. South Carolina now has dozens of reef sites, and the agency makes their location data available as a free download for marine GPS devices so fishing and diving vessels may discover them.You use AI every day. articles.title: A shopkeeper in rural Australia took over a 145-year-old store just 10 months ago; while clearing an old freezer, Ash Stanbridge found a Magnum Ego ice cream from the late 1990s still frozen and intact
articles.summary: A shopkeeper in rural Australia has stumbled upon a piece of 1990s nostalgia while cleaning an old freezer, discovering a Magnum Ego ice cream believed to
articles.body: A shopkeeper in rural Australia has stumbled upon a piece of 1990s nostalgia while cleaning an old freezer, discovering a Magnum Ego ice cream believed to date back nearly three decades. Ash Stanbridge, who took over the historic Kolmar House General Store in Harrow, Victoria, just 10 months ago, found the packaged ice cream buried beneath layers of ice, where it had remained frozen and intact.According to ABC News Australia, which reported the discovery on October 24, Stanbridge was routinely defrosting and cleaning an old freezer when he noticed an unfamiliar object beneath the ice. The old Magnum logo and wrapper caught his attention, prompting him to realise that the product had likely been there for years. The shopkeeper said he was initially amazed and struggled to believe what he had found.The discovery has since attracted widespread attention online, with Australians sharing memories of the discontinued ice cream and calling for its return. The find is particularly striking because the store itself has more than 145 years of history, having served generations of residents in the small Victorian town.A childhood favourite hidden beneath decades of iceThe ice cream was identified as Magnum Ego, a product introduced in Australia in 1998. It featured vanilla ice cream coated with a layer of milk chocolate, a caramel layer and an outer chocolate shell, making it a particularly indulgent variation of the familiar Magnum ice cream bar. For Stanbridge, the discovery brought back memories of growing up in the late 1990s, when the product was considered a premium treat.Speaking to ABC News, he recalled family trips to service stations to buy ice cream and described the Ego as a top-tier product that people were excited about. He said seeing its old packaging immediately brought those memories back.The product's reported origins in the late 1990s make the discovery especially remarkable. However, the exact manufacturing date of the individual ice cream has not been independently established. Its age is based on the packaging and the shopkeeper's recollections rather than a verified production record.Stanbridge said the ice cream was still solid and intact when he uncovered it. Despite the curiosity surrounding the find, he was not willing to taste it, according to ABC News.Historic store yields other forgotten productsThe Magnum Ego was not the only unexpected discovery during the clean-out. Stanbridge also found old packets of chips believed to date from the 1980s and 1990s, as well as a sealed flavoured-milk container that no longer contained any liquid.The items were found in the same storeroom as the freezer and offered a glimpse into the shop's earlier years. Rather than immediately throwing everything away, Stanbridge decided to retain many of the objects as part of the store's history.The Kolmar House General Store is located in Harrow, a rural township in south-west Victoria. Its long history predates Stanbridge's ownership by well over a century. According to *Real Commercial*, the building is more than 145 years old, and the business has been a longstanding part of the local community.The discovery also highlights how older stock and forgotten objects can remain hidden in storage spaces when businesses change hands. Although Stanbridge had only recently taken over the store, the freezer and its contents had been left behind by previous owners.Magnum responds as nostalgia spreads onlineAfter sharing the discovery on social media, Stanbridge saw the find attract attention from people who remembered the ice cream from their childhoods. Comments included recollections of buying the product regularly and disappointment that it was no longer available.The Magnum Ice Cream Company, which Stanbridge contacted about the discovery, acknowledged the response and said it was following the conversation. "Australians have been sharing stories, memories and tributes to Magnum Ego, reminding us just how special the product remains to so many people," the company told ABC News.It added that it had enjoyed hearing people's memories of the ice cream and said, "For now, all we can say is watch this space."The product was discontinued earlier in 2026, according to ABC News, adding to the significance of the discovery for its fans. The company's response, however, should not be interpreted as confirmation that the ice cream will return to Australian shelves.The Magnum Ego find has become more than an unusual freezer discovery. It has revived memories of a product associated with family outings, summer treats and a particular period in Australian food culture.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Fireworks, flags and celebrations as student-led movement wins in Serbia; can they deliver reforms?
articles.summary: Celebrations swept across Serbia after Gen Z-backed candidates defeated president Aleksandar Vucic’s ruling party in a historic election, ending his long
articles.body: Celebrations swept across Serbia after Gen Z-backed candidates defeated president Aleksandar Vucic’s ruling party in a historic election, ending his long grip on power. In Belgrade, crowds filled central squares, cars draped in Serbian flags honked their horns and fireworks lit up the sky as jubilant protesters dismantled barricades around a pro-government encampment near parliament.But beyond the celebrations, a key question remains: Can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change?The election follows nearly two years of student-led demonstrations sparked by the collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station in 2024, which killed 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and cronyism for the disaster, turning the tragedy into a wider campaign for accountability.From street protests to political powerVisuals circulating on social media showed crowds taking to the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian cities soon after the election results were announced. The student movement built nationwide support without a single leader and eventually fielded 250 candidates, including academics, lawyers, doctors, farmers, actors and musicians.Its agenda centres on anti-corruption measures, judicial reform and stronger public institutions. The candidates have proposed an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors, transparent appointments to state-owned companies and tighter scrutiny of public infrastructure contracts.However, unity could prove difficult once the movement begins governing.“(The student movement created) such a shift in Serbia's culture; we will just have to see if it lasts,” Katarina Popovic, a professor at the University of Belgrade told news agency Reuters.“We just hope that there are big goals that can keep them together long enough to deconstruct the system,” she added.Can the new government deliver reforms?Under Serbia’s constitution, the student-backed candidates have 90 days to form a government after parliament is convened following the announcement of final election results.The immediate challenges include passing a year-end budget, addressing rising public and private debt, reforming the police and intelligence services, and strengthening the judiciary.The students' victory "is likely to trigger broad institutional and policy changes centred on anti-corruption, the rule of law, and better public services. However, bureaucratic resistance to reforms and the movement’s limited governing experience could make the transition challenging," Teneo Global Research said in a report on Monday.The IMF projects Serbia’s economy to grow 3 per cent in 2026 and 4 per cent in 2027, while inflation rose to 4.1 per cent in September from 2.2 per cent in August. The central bank has held its benchmark interest rate at 5.75 per cent since 2024.“The new government would have to fight its corner,” warned Bozo Prelevic, a Belgrade-based lawyer and former co-minister of the interior, referring to the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which is expected to remain a formidable opposition force.The movement has also promised economic changes, including action against retail monopolies to lower food prices, tax relief for lower-income groups, affordable housing initiatives and cheaper medicines.Kosovo, Russia and the European UnionForeign policy could be another test. The student-backed candidates oppose recognising Kosovo’s independence, declared in 2008, while relations with the European Union remain strained over stalled accession talks and the need to normalise ties with Pristina.The movement has also said it does not intend to impose sanctions on Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and a major gas supplier. At the same time, the European Commission has offered support for reforms involving the rule of law and media freedom.“I am sure (the Student List) will find a way, just as they have so far, to choose someone capable of governing,” said Savo Manojlovic of the student-friendly Move-Change movement, according to Reuters.You use AI every day.
